question: What is the HOST submission cost of a decode step's 784 launches versus one hipGraphLaunch of the captured chain - the ceiling X7 can aim at before any engine wiring?
method: 784 hipMemsetAsync ops on a dedicated capture stream (the legacy default stream cannot capture - HIP error 900): timed as direct launches, then captured once, instantiated, and replayed 50x with a drain before each timed replay so queue backpressure is excluded from the timed region.
readings: Graph replay removes ~99% of host submission time at decode launch counts (1423 -> 12.5 us).
Without the drain-before-timing, replay medians bimodal at ~2-3 ms: that is device backpressure from the synthetic 784 MB chain, not graph cost - engine-side measurements must pace the same way.
WALL ceiling stays bounded by the committed wall-minus-busy gap (~1.7 ms/step): launch host time overlaps device work today.
Integration fact: capture needs a non-default stream; gemma4's wrappers all default to stream 0, so wiring X7 means threading an explicit stream through _forward_block_inner.

Design question for the build: kernels whose grid scales with context length (global-layer attention tiles) break stable capture; the existing gguf_decode_graph module solves the analogous problem for qwen35 with device-side scalar recording (record_i64_scalar_indexed / advance_decode_position_i64) - port that pattern rather than recapture per step (recapture would re-issue the very launches replay is meant to save).
